source.author: ov
source.text: cumque suis Gryneus immanem sustulit aram ignibus et medium Lapitharum iecit in agmen depressitque duos, Brotean et Orion: Orio mater erat Mycale, quam deduxisse canendo saepe reluctantis constabat cornua lunae.
source.text_original: cumque suis Gryneus immanem sustulit aram / ignibus et medium Lapitharum iecit in agmen / depressitque duos, Brotean et Orion: Orio / mater erat Mycale, quam deduxisse canendo / saepe reluctantis constabat cornua lunae.
source.text_english: And when Gryneus had raised his huge altar with his own fires and hurled it into the middle of the Lapiths’ ranks and crushed two men, Broteas and Orion, Orion’s mother was Mycale, who, it was established, had often by her chanting drawn down the horns of the reluctant moon.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: crateres mensaeque volant araeque deorum poculaque, insignis veterum labor.
reuse.text_original: crateres mensaeque volant araeque deorum / poculaque, insignis veterum labor.
reuse.text_english: craters and tables and altars of the gods fly about, and cups, a notable workmanship of the ancients.
